question: Will the FAA type-certify the Boeing 737 MAX 10 before 2027?

calls.reasoning: The FAA Type Certification Board completed its final review on Oct 16, 2026, and multiple Reuters-sourced reports (Oct 19-20) say Transportation Secretary Duffy is announcing the 737 MAX 10 certification at Everett on Oct 20. The late-September FMC software anomaly was ruled not an unsafe condition and handled with a non-mandatory SAIB, so it is not blocking. If the certificate is issued before the question closes, the question is annulled; conditional on it being scored, issuance after close but before Jan 1, 2027 is near-certain. The remaining risk is a last-minute snag that delays signing more than about 10 weeks. No human prediction market was found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.

- Multiple outlets (Spokesman, Investing.com, US News, 2026-10-19/20) repeat the Reuters report; the FAA Type Certification Board held its final review Fri Oct 16, 2026.
- Aviacionline (Oct 2026): after the TCB, Boeing must submit the Project Statement of Completion before the TC signatures; the FMC U14/U14.1 software anomaly was judged not an unsafe condition, and non-mandatory SAIB 2026-17 was issued.
- Aviation Week (late Sep/Oct 2026): FAA says the software issue will not stop 737-10 certification.
- Leeham (2026-10-06, 10-19): path to certification clear; Boeing hoping to secure it ahead of its earnings report.
- Flight testing: 976 flights, 2,060+ hours; final certification flight July 28, 2026. First deliveries targeted for 2027.
- Precedent: MAX 7 certified Aug 2026 after an 8-year review. Prior MAX 10 delays: engine anti-ice issue (2023), FMC glitch (Sep 2026).
- A GuruFocus headline says the MAX 10 'Receives FAA Approval' (page returned 403; not verified).
- Status quo: certificate issuance imminent as of 2026-10-20.
- Resolution: resolves off an FAA amended TC (FAA Newsroom), not a Boeing statement. Issuance BEFORE question close means the question is annulled; only issuance after close and before 2027-01-01 counts as Yes.
- Event window: question close -> 2026-12-31 per the criteria; as of 2026-10-20 the window has essentially just begun (~0% elapsed, ~72 days remain).
- Searched but not found: any Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmaker market; FAA Newsroom confirmation of the actual TC signing.
